::: {#exm-connected-component}
#### The components of the cut office

The graph $H$ of @exr-cut-cables has two connected components (@def-connected-component):
the subgraph with vertices $a, b, c$ and the three edges among them,
and the subgraph with vertices $d, e, f$ and the three edges among them.
Each of them is connected, and each already has every edge of $H$ between its vertices.
A connected subgraph of $H$ that contained $a$ and one of $d$, $e$, $f$ would have a walk from $a$ to that vertex,
and @sol-cut-cables showed that a walk from $a$ in $H$ stays in $\set{a, b, c}$.
The same argument from $d$ shows that no connected subgraph contains $d$ and one of $a$, $b$, $c$.

A connected graph, such as the office graph, has one connected component: the whole graph.

:::
